summary.title: LoopArena: Benchmarking Models as Runtime Controllers for Loop Engineering

details: In 'Loop Engineering', a model manages the successive rounds of a long-running coding agent, but existing coding benchmarks score the complete agent system rather than the model doing the managing.
Isolating loop-control ability requires holding the coding executor fixed so the only varying component is the controlling model.

LoopArena: a benchmark that evaluates a model as a Controller in a two-agent harness where a fixed Worker does all coding; after each Worker segment a temporary Reporter (same model/history as Worker, read-only) summarizes progress into a deterministically formatted Evidence Packet, and the Controller responds with a structured Loop Contract (advance / verify / stop plus a bounded next Worker assignment).

Three evaluation settings at different execution scopes: Type I (a single frozen four-way Loop Contract choice whose correct option is established by executing candidates during benchmark construction), Type II (closed-loop control over a task slice from a prepared intermediate workspace), Type III (closed-loop control over the paired full long-horizon task).
Tasks drawn from SlopCodeBench (SCBench, long-horizon iterative coding) and BeyondSWE; 27 unique full tasks (11 SCBench / 16 BeyondSWE) used for both Type III and their paired Type II slices.

90 Type I questions (40 SCBench / 50 BeyondSWE), each anchored at a restorable control point with the recorded Contract plus three authored plausible alternatives, frozen in neutral order before any replay.
Type II slices retained only if the starting workspace fails at least one stage requirement and the source completed state passes all requirements through that stage.

All four candidates replayed from the same restored state under two predeclared matched schedules (same Worker, budget, evaluator, stopping rules, seeds S+1e6 and S+2e6; only the initial Contract differs).

Winner rule: terminal task success first; ties broken by fewer downstream control cycles, then fewer Worker turns; item kept only if both schedules yield the same unique winner, else rejected (no post-hoc candidate rewriting).
Post-freeze LLM-assisted and expert audits check clarity, plausibility and leakage but cannot override the replay-defined answer.
Shared Worker and Reporter model: Qwen3.7-Plus; Worker is the only component with coding tools and runs a native ReAct loop; Controller has no repository access.
Limits: 600 Worker ReAct turns or 7,200s per episode, at most 128 control cycles, 86,400s cumulative, 50-turn Reporter cap; Controller output cap 20,480 tokens, Worker/Reporter 8,192.
K=3 repeats per task and policy; per-run averages: Type II 51-80 Worker turns and ~3-4 control cycles, Type III 140-289 turns and ~9-13 cycles.
Evaluated Controllers: Qwen3.7-Plus, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, GLM 5.2, GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8 (temperature 0 or provider-default thinking).

Reference policies (not ranked): no control (Worker runs autonomously once) and fixed control (deterministically restates the same goal at every handoff, stopping when Worker declares 'Goal complete.').

Metrics: Contract Accuracy and Invalid Rate (Type I); Strict Success Rate over tasks x 3 runs, with SCBench Core checks or BeyondSWE Harbor reward 1 (Type II/III); estimated no-cache inference cost from a frozen public price schedule; Spearman rho between Type II and Type III Controller orderings.
Type I deterministic shortcut baselines: uniform random, majority position, action-only, shortest candidate, lexical Packet-candidate overlap.
SCBench scoring sensitivity: Core checks (main) vs all checks vs all non-error checks.
Protocol-failure analysis of Controller output-limit exhaustion and invalid Contracts (167 DeepSeek/GLM evaluations); run-to-run stability across the three repeats.

key_findings.finding: Full-task runtime loop control is far from solved, and merely persisting the goal is not real control.
key_findings.evidence: Type III Strict Success Rate spans 16.05% (GLM 5.2) to 24.69% (GPT-5.5); fixed control raises Type II success from 39.51% to 46.91% over no control but ties no control at 18.52% on Type III, while model Controllers reach up to 24.69%.

key_findings.finding: The task-slice setting (Type II) reproduces the full-task Controller ordering at substantially lower cost.
key_findings.evidence: Paired Type II inference cost is 64.4% lower on average than Type III; Spearman rho between the two orderings is 0.9747 under the Core criterion, with zero strict rank reversals among the nine strictly ordered Controller pairs (one pair tied).

key_findings.finding: Type I contract selection discriminates Controllers without any Worker execution and is not solvable by surface shortcuts.
key_findings.evidence: Contract Accuracy ranges 72.22% (Qwen3.7-Plus) to 87.78% (GPT-5.5) with 0% invalid responses; the best deterministic shortcut (majority position) reaches only 31.11%, and uniform, action-only, length, and lexical-overlap rules score 25.00% or lower.

key_findings.finding: Controller ranking on executable settings is sensitive to the underlying task success criterion.
key_findings.evidence: Under all-checks and all-non-error SCBench scoring, Type II-Type III rank correlation collapses to 0.1481 and -0.2962 respectively, and Type III SSR ranges compress to 16.05-17.28%, versus rho=0.9747 under the Core criterion.

key_findings.finding: Loop control incurs real overhead and protocol-failure modes that vary sharply by Controller.
key_findings.evidence: Type III cost per run ranges from $4.86 (GLM 5.2) to $18.84 (GPT-5.5) versus $2.01 for no control; across 167 DeepSeek/GLM evaluations, 162/1,614 Controller calls hit the 20,480-token output limit (20.39% of GLM Type III calls vs 1.69% for DeepSeek), counted as failures.
